title: Layers: wrapping a message and unwrapping it
intro: A chat message 'Hi' crosses the internet in layers. Each layer adds its own label going down. Can you spot who adds the IP address?

predict.question: Going down the stack, which layer adds the IP addresses?
predict.reveal: The Internet layer wraps the segment in an IP header with source and destination addresses so routers can forward it.

takeaway: Going down, each layer wraps the data in its own header (encapsulation); going up, each layer strips its header (decapsulation).

steps.say: TCP/IP has 4 layers (OSI splits them into 7). Your phone sends 'Hi' to a friend. It travels down 4 layers, across the wire, then up 4 layers.

cards.title: Application
cards.text: Your app makes the message: Hi

cards.title: Transport
cards.text: TCP adds ports and a sequence number

cards.title: Internet
cards.text: IP adds source and destination address

steps.say: Application layer: the chat app creates the data, just the text Hi, using a protocol like HTTP. No addressing yet.

cards.title: Transport
cards.text: TCP adds ports and a sequence number

cards.title: Internet
cards.text: IP adds source and destination address

steps.say: Transport layer: TCP adds a header with port numbers (which app) and a sequence number. Data plus header is now a segment.

cards.title: Internet
cards.text: IP adds source and destination address

steps.say: Internet layer: IP adds a header with your IP and your friend's IP. Now it is a packet that routers can forward across networks.
Link layer: adds a frame header with MAC addresses for the next hop, plus a check value at the end. The frame becomes bits on the wire.
Routers along the way peel only the link and IP layers to choose the next hop, then re-wrap. At last the frame reaches your friend's phone.
Receiver link layer: checks the MAC address and check value, strips the frame header and passes the packet up.
Internet layer: confirms the destination IP is mine, strips the IP header, and hands the segment up.
Transport layer: TCP checks the sequence number, uses the port to pick the right app, strips its header, and hands up the data.

cards.title: Transport
cards.text: Port picks the chat app, header removed

steps.say: Application layer: the chat app receives plain Hi. Each layer only read its own header, like unwrapping nested gift boxes.

cards.title: Transport
cards.text: Port picks the chat app, header removed
